title: Role-Based Access Boundaries
purpose: Show the four concentric role boundaries (Unauthenticated, Fan, Creator, Admin) and what each role can access in terms of route groups, UI features, and data. Overlay the access control gaps.
audience: Security engineers, backend developers, architects, compliance team
description: Four concentric trust zones mapping what each role can access. Unauthenticated users can access auth routes, public content, and analytics logging. Fans can browse/search creators, view profiles, subscribe (crypto), view subscriber content, purchase PPV, send tips, message subscribed creators, enter contests, refer friends, report content, and create support tickets. Creators inherit all fan capabilities plus upload content, AI captions, earnings dashboard, payouts, content management, broadcast, contests, subscriber analytics, subscription tiers, referral codes, and Enclave applications. Admins inherit all capabilities plus impersonation, dashboard (5 parallel queries), user management, content moderation, support tickets, platform settings, verification document viewing, and custom reports. Security gaps: No fan route guard (frontend /fan/* routes accessible to unauthenticated users), 2 unprotected referral routes (no protect middleware), and impersonation boundary bypass with no audit trail.

preconditions: User has a valid account with assigned role (fan, creator, or admin)
Authentication and authorization middleware is configured on backend routes

postconditions: User is redirected to role-appropriate landing page after authentication
Access to unauthorized features returns 401/403 on backend and redirects on frontend

connections.label: Unauthenticated user signs up or logs in to become fan
Fan completes creator onboarding and verification to become creator
Creator elevated to admin by platform operator
Guest analytics events logged via optionalProtect
Fan routes lack guard — UI accessible without auth

validationRules: Fan routes (/fan/*) in frontend lack withAuthGuard — security gap
Creator routes require protectAndCreator middleware chain
Admin routes require protectAndAdmin middleware chain (router-level)
Auth routes (signup, login, forgot-password) have no auth middleware
Some public routes use optionalProtect (analytics, profile view)
businessRules: Role hierarchy: Unauthenticated < Fan < Creator < Admin
Each role inherits all capabilities of roles below it
Creator needs onboarding + verification for full access (creators with incomplete onboarding are restricted)
Admin impersonation bypasses all role checks — admin acts as the impersonated user
securityConsiderations: CRITICAL: No fan route guard — unauthenticated users can access /fan/* UI (UI leaks)
CRITICAL: 2 unprotected referral routes accessible without any authentication
CRITICAL: Impersonation has no audit trail — no logging of impersonated actions
JWT tokens stored in localStorage — vulnerable to XSS attacks
Admin inherits all capabilities, including the ability to send emails to any user via admin messaging
performanceConsiderations: Admin dashboard runs 5 parallel Promise.all queries per page load — no caching
Creator dashboard aggregates multiple data sources — potential slow load for popular creators
annotations: GAP: No fan route guard — frontend /fan/* routes lack withAuthGuard, UI accessible to unauthenticated users
GAP: 2 unprotected referral routes — /api/v1/referrals/* has no protect middleware
GAP: Impersonation boundary bypass — admin can impersonate any user with no audit trail
